subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 8: Literacy – Reading an information text
outcomes: Match fact files to information texts.
Find facts quickly using headings like Home, Food and Size.
Answer questions about animals in complete sentences.

tf.s: A vertebrate is an animal with a backbone.
The giant prickly stick insect is a vertebrate.
tf.why: It is an insect, so it is an invertebrate.

tf.s: The mata mata turtle is a reptile.
The stick insect lives in the forests of Australia.
tf.why: Yes, its home is in Australian forests.

tf.s: The mata mata turtle lives in cold seas near the North Pole.
tf.why: It lives in warm lakes, ponds and rivers in South America.

tf.s: The stick insect can hide easily because it looks like dead leaves or wood.
tf.why: Yes, its shape and colour help it hide.

tf.s: The turtle uses its long nose to breathe while it hides in the water.
tf.why: Yes, it breathes through its long nose.

tf.s: A fact file explains facts in long paragraphs.
tf.why: A fact file gives short notes under headings.

tf.s: The stick insect can be up to 20 metres long.
tf.why: It is up to 20 centimetres long.

tf.s: Both the stick insect and the mata mata turtle lay eggs.
tf.why: Yes, that is one way they are the same.

boxes.q: Is the mata mata turtle a vertebrate or an invertebrate?
What does the mata mata turtle eat?
boxes.why: Its food is fish and small animals.

boxes.q: How much does the stick insect weigh?
boxes.why: It is very light: up to 20 grams.

boxes.q: What colour is the stick insect's body?
boxes.why: Brown or green helps it look like leaves.

boxes.q: Which heading tells you where an animal lives?
boxes.why: Home tells us where it lives.

boxes.q: An animal without a backbone is …
boxes.why: In- means it has no backbone.

boxes.q: Which continent is the mata mata turtle from?
What kind of animal is the stick insect?
boxes.why: It is an insect, with no backbone.

boxes.q: Which helps you find facts fast in a fact file?
boxes.why: Headings show where each fact is.

boxes.q: Which answer is a complete sentence?
o: It lives in the forests of Australia.
boxes.why: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb.

Home of the mata mata turtle

mcq.q: What is the main difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate?
mcq.why: The backbone is the key difference.

mcq.q: Where does the mata mata turtle live?
o: in warm lakes, ponds and rivers
mcq.why: It lives in warm fresh water in South America.

mcq.q: Which of these is a fact file heading?
mcq.why: Fact files use headings like Family, Food and Home.

mcq.q: What does the mata mata turtle use its long nose for?
o: to breathe while it hides in the water
mcq.why: It stays hidden and breathes through its nose.

mcq.q: Answer in a complete sentence: How much does the stick insect weigh?
o: The stick insect weighs up to 20 grams.
mcq.why: A full answer repeats the subject and the verb.

mcq.q: Correct the sentence: The mata mata turtle is an invertebrate.
o: The mata mata turtle is a vertebrate reptile.
The mata mata turtle is an insect.
The mata mata turtle is an invertebrate insect.
The mata mata turtle is a bird.
mcq.why: Turtles are reptiles with a backbone.

mcq.q: You want to know what the stick insect eats. Which heading do you look at?
mcq.why: Food tells you what it eats.

mcq.q: Why is it easy for the stick insect to hide?
o: It looks like dead leaves or wood.
mcq.why: Its shape and colour are like the forest.

mcq.q: Which sentence shows one similarity and one difference?
o: Both lay eggs, but the turtle is a vertebrate and the stick insect is not.
Both are vertebrates and both live in Australia.
Both are insects, but only one lays eggs.
Both live in water, but the turtle is green.
mcq.why: Good comparison with true facts from the texts.

mcq.q: Why does an information text use full sentences but a fact file doesn't?
o: A fact file gives quick notes; a text explains facts.
A fact file is for teachers only.
An information text has no facts.
A fact file is always longer.
mcq.why: Notes are quick; texts explain in sentences.
